verdict.rationale: CoreWeave's own Capacity Finder in the Cloud Console lets users compare placement availability across Zones for one or more GPU and CPU instance types and a requested Node count before creating a Spot Node Pool, which covers the core of checking availability by type and location before provisioning. The documentation places it only in the Spot Node Pool workflow. It does not say the data is real-time, and it describes no programmatic or API access. missing for 10: explicit real-time freshness of availability data, coverage for On-Demand/reserved provisioning beyond Spot, region-level (not just Zone) view, API/CLI access to availability, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ML engineer, I can see real-time GPU availability by type and region before I try to provision, instead of discovering stockouts by failure

citations.quote: Before you create a Spot Node Pool, use Capacity Finder in the Cloud Console to compare placement availability across Zones for your requested instance type and Node count.
use Capacity Finder in the Cloud Console to compare placement availability across Zones for one or more GPU and CPU instance types
